I found no real deviations, so the model passes. The numeric check passed: all 743 nodes matched the dataset (79 spaces, 85 openings, 2 connectors, 505 assets), with no failures or warnings. The largest error was about 3e-6 m in space position; every other error was zero. Ground floor (level 0): the room layout matches the dataset plan. That covers the 5×3 grid of halls (H-A, H-B and H-C, rows 1 to 5, with H-A5/B5/C5 sticking out to the north), the office rooms 0.19–0.33 west of corridor 0.16, and rooms 0.17, 0.18 and 0.34–0.47 to its east. After scaling, each room's height along the strip matches the dataset. The four outside doors match: the top of H-B5, the top of corridor 0.16, and the west walls of H-C3 and H-C2. The side doors from 0.33 to H-A4 and from 0.19 to H-A1 are in the right places. Equipment sits in the H-A and H-C halls and the offices; the grey H-B halls have little or none, which fits their role as walkways. Floor 1 (level 1): rooms 1.04–1.18 west of corridor 1.01 and rooms 1.02, 1.03 and 1.19–1.32 east of it match the dataset in order and size. Most of the hall-to-hall doors and the office doors onto the corridors are too small to read in the generated images, so I couldn't check them by eye; for those I'm relying on the numeric check, which found zero error for all 85 openings. The other differences I saw are only colours, fills and labels.
